_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Luxembourg covering County of Luxembourg (963 CE, Siegfried I), House of Luxembourg (3 Holy Roman Emperors), Burgundian/Habsburg/Spanish/French/Dutch rule, Congress of Vienna 1815, independence 1839 (Treaty of London), Grand Duchy, perpetual neutrality, occupied in both World Wars, Benelux, EU founding member (1952 ECSC), financial centre, and modern cosmopolitan microstate.

religion.note: Historically Catholic; rapid secularisation; state-church separation 2015 (ended 1801 Concordat); religious classes replaced by values education in schools; diverse religious landscape due to massive immigration; Echternach dancing procession (UNESCO, unique hopping pilgrimage since 7th century)

ethnic_groups.name: Luxembourgish
ethnic_groups.notes: Minority in own country (lowest native percentage in EU); trilingual by education (Luxembourgish + French + German); strong national identity despite small size; 'Mir wëlle bleiwe wat mir sinn' ('We want to remain what we are', national motto); concern about cultural dilution

ethnic_groups.name: Portuguese
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest foreign community; arrived from 1960s (steel/construction); 3rd generation integrating; largest Portuguese community per capita outside Portugal; Festa Portuguesa celebrated

ethnic_groups.name: French
ethnic_groups.notes: Cross-border workers (200k+ commute daily from France/Belgium/Germany); residents; French dominant working language

ethnic_groups.name: Italian
ethnic_groups.notes: Steel industry workers; post-WWII immigration; oldest immigrant community

ethnic_groups.name: Other
ethnic_groups.notes: German, British (post-Brexit relocations), Indian, Chinese, Montenegrin, Cape Verdean; 170+ nationalities; ~47% foreign-born (highest in EU); 200,000+ daily cross-border commuters

independence.from: Netherlands (Treaty of London; first independence 1815 as Grand Duchy under Dutch crown)

country_profile.notes_unique: EU capital (de facto: European Court of Justice, European Investment Bank, Eurostat, Court of Auditors, Secretariat of European Parliament; alongside Brussels/Strasbourg); highest GDP per capita in world (nominal, but inflated by cross-border commuters counted in GDP but not population); financial centre (largest investment fund domicile in Europe, second globally after US; 143 banks; fintech hub); steel legacy (ARBED/ArcelorMittal, world's largest steel company, founded here); only Grand Duchy remaining in world; Luxembourgish language (Franconian/Moselle dialect, national language since 1984, identity marker); Battle of the Bulge 1944-45 (Ardennes, devastating, Luxembourg liberated by Americans); Schengen Agreement signed here (1985, town of Schengen); Luxembourg City fortifications UNESCO ('Gibraltar of the North'); trilingual education system (Luxembourgish in kindergarten, German in primary, French in secondary); RTL Group (largest European broadcaster, founded here); free public transport (first country in world, 2020)

current_leader.name: Grand Duke Henri
current_leader.title: Grand Duke
current_leader.notes: House of Nassau-Weilburg/Bourbon-Parma; constitutional monarch; succeeded father Jean; refused to sign euthanasia law 2008 (constitutional amendment removed requirement for royal assent); military education (Sandhurst); popular; married to Cuban-born Grand Duchess María Teresa

prime_minister.name: Luc Frieden
prime_minister.title: Prime Minister
prime_minister.notes: CSV (Christian Social People's Party); former finance minister/justice minister; coalition with DP (Democrats); returned to politics after private sector (banking/BIL); conservative; financial regulation expertise; succeeded Bettel

former_leaders.name: Xavier Bettel
former_leaders.notes: DP (Democrats); first openly gay PM in EU to marry in office (2015); liberal coalition; moderniser; made public transport free (2020, first in world); cultural liberalisation; 2 terms; lost 2023 election

former_leaders.name: Jean-Claude Juncker
former_leaders.notes: CSV; 18 years PM (longest in EU at time); 'Mr. Europe'; Eurogroup president (2005-13); European Commission President (2014-19); euro crisis management; master dealmaker; controversial personal style; alcoholism rumours; defined Luxembourg's EU position

former_leaders.name: Grand Duke Jean
former_leaders.notes: WWII volunteer (Irish Guards, Normandy landings); popular; abdicated in favour of son Henri; died 2019 aged 98; seen as embodiment of modern Luxembourg

910.name: Roman Era in the Luxembourg Region
910.description: The area of present-day Luxembourg lay within the Roman provinces of Gallia Belgica and later Germania Superior, with Roman villas, roads, and the settlement at Dalheim (Ricciacum) attesting to integration into the empire.

sub_clusters.name: Roman Villas & Settlements
sub_clusters.description: Archaeological evidence of Roman villas, the vicus at Dalheim, road networks connecting Trier and Reims, and the transition to Frankish settlement in late antiquity.

920.name: County of Luxembourg
920.description: Count Siegfried's acquisition of Lucilinburhuc castle in 963 CE founded the County of Luxembourg, which produced four Holy Roman Emperors and became one of the most powerful territories in the medieval Low Countries.

sub_clusters.name: Siegfried & Castle Foundation
sub_clusters.description: Count Siegfried I's acquisition of Lucilinburhuc ('little fortress') on the Bock promontory in 963, founding the dynasty and the fortress that would define Luxembourg's identity.
key_events: Count Siegfried acquires Lucilinburhuc castle (963 CE)

sub_clusters.name: Luxembourg Emperors of the HRE
sub_clusters.description: The House of Luxembourg's remarkable ascent, producing Emperors Henry VII, Charles IV (Golden Bull of 1356), Wenceslaus, and Sigismund, making it one of Europe's most powerful dynasties.

sub_clusters.name: Burgundian Acquisition
sub_clusters.description: The duchy's decline and sale to Philip the Good of Burgundy in 1443, integrating Luxembourg into the Burgundian Netherlands.

930.name: Habsburg Rule & the 'Gibraltar of the North'
930.description: Under successive Habsburg, Spanish, French, and Austrian rulers, Luxembourg's fortress was continuously expanded by Vauban and others, earning it the epithet 'Gibraltar of the North' as one of Europe's most formidable strongholds.

sub_clusters.name: Spanish Habsburg & Fortress Expansion
sub_clusters.description: Luxembourg under Spanish Habsburg rule, Vauban's siege and capture for Louis XIV (1684), and the fortress's growing strategic importance in European power politics.

sub_clusters.name: Austrian Habsburg Period
sub_clusters.description: Transfer to Austrian Habsburgs at Utrecht (1713), continued fortress development, and French Revolutionary annexation ending centuries of foreign rule.
key_events: Vauban captures Luxembourg fortress for Louis XIV (1684)

940.name: Grand Duchy & Path to Independence
940.description: The Congress of Vienna created the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg in personal union with the Netherlands. The Belgian Revolution, the London Conferences, and the 1867 Treaty of London established Luxembourg as a perpetually neutral, independent state.

sub_clusters.name: Congress of Vienna & Grand Duchy
sub_clusters.description: Creation of the Grand Duchy under William I of the Netherlands, the Luxembourg Crisis during the Belgian Revolution, and the Treaty of London (1839) partitioning the territory.

sub_clusters.name: Luxembourg Crisis & Treaty of London (1867)
sub_clusters.description: The Franco-Prussian diplomatic crisis over Luxembourg (1867), the Second Treaty of London establishing perpetual neutrality, dismantling of the fortress, and the end of personal union with the Netherlands in 1890.
key_events: Treaty of London establishes Luxembourg's perpetual neutrality (1867)
Personal union with the Netherlands ends; Grand Duchy fully independent (1890)

950.name: World Wars & German Occupation
950.description: Despite its guaranteed neutrality, Luxembourg was occupied by Germany in both World Wars. WWII brought forced Germanisation, conscription of Luxembourgers into the Wehrmacht, and eventual liberation by American forces.

sub_clusters.name: WWI German Occupation
sub_clusters.description: German occupation despite neutrality, Grand Duchess Marie-Adélaïde's controversial accommodation, her forced abdication, and the post-war referendum confirming the monarchy and independence.

sub_clusters.name: WWII Annexation & Resistance
sub_clusters.description: Nazi Germany's annexation and forced Germanisation, the 1942 general strike against conscription, forced enrolment of Luxembourgers into the Wehrmacht, and liberation during the Battle of the Bulge.
key_events: Luxembourg general strike against Nazi forced conscription (1942)
Battle of the Bulge – liberation by US forces (1944–1945)

950.name: ECSC Founding & European Construction
950.description: Luxembourg played a founding role in European integration, with Robert Schuman (born in Luxembourg) proposing the ECSC, and Luxembourg City becoming home to key European institutions.

sub_clusters.name: Schuman Declaration & ECSC
sub_clusters.description: Robert Schuman's declaration (1950), the founding of the European Coal and Steel Community (1952) with institutions based in Luxembourg, and the Treaty of Rome establishing the EEC.
key_events: Schuman Declaration proposes European Coal and Steel Community (1950)

960.name: EU Institutions & Financial Hub
960.description: Luxembourg evolved into a major EU institutional seat and Europe's leading investment fund domicile, while maintaining its distinctive multilingual identity (Luxembourgish, French, German) and Grand Ducal traditions.

sub_clusters.name: European Institutional Capital
sub_clusters.description: Luxembourg as host of the European Court of Justice, European Investment Bank, Court of Auditors, and Eurostat, cementing its role in EU governance.

sub_clusters.name: Banking Centre & Modern Identity
sub_clusters.description: Rise as Europe's premier investment fund centre, the LuxLeaks tax scandal (2014), adoption of Luxembourgish as a national language (1984), and the multicultural society where nearly half the population are foreign nationals.
